insight: Microservices success is fundamentally about organizational structure, not technology choices like Docker or Kubernetes
Amazon's two-pizza rule limits teams to 6-8 members (size that two pizzas can feed)
Team communication links grow by formula (n * n-1) / 2, causing communication to degrade as teams grow
J Richard Hackman's research found optimal team size is less than 10 members
Conway's Law states organizations design systems that mirror their communication structures
Cross-functional teams must include developers, DBAs, QA, and operations on the same team to prevent 'throwing over the fence'
Prematurely breaking apps into microservices without proper organizational structure can lead to 'SOA on steroids disaster'
Jeff Bezos stated 'Communication is terrible' when managers requested more team communication, emphasizing effective over frequent communication
Small microservices teams behave like open-source projects with developers, testers, and ops working together
SOA had similar principles to microservices but lost focus by getting caught up in WS-* specs rather than organizational goals
Navy Seals work in combat teams of 4 people
Author plans to discuss OpenShift and fabric8io tooling in a future post
